title: Bootstrap: Wails v2 app shell, SQLite+AES-GCM, Smart Recovery, sidebar scaffold
design: Stack: Go + Wails v2 + React + TypeScript. Initialize Go module, Wails v2 project. On first launch: generate 256-bit AES-GCM key (app.key) beside binary. On subsequent launch: check app.key exists; if missing but SQLite exists, show Smart Recovery modal (Cancel = exit, Reset & Re-init = wipe SQLite + generate new key). SQLite schema: server_profiles, catalog_objects, app_last_op. Sidebar navigation scaffold: Servers | Backup | Restore | Settings — panels empty, routing wired. All app files in Executable Scope (os.Executable() dir). Wails v2, single window.
acceptance_criteria: app launches, app.key created on first run, Smart Recovery modal appears when app.key deleted with existing SQLite, sidebar navigation switches panels without crash

title: Backup workflow: multi-DB sequential mariadb-dump with progress
design: UI: select Server Profile -> connect -> SHOW DATABASES filtered (hide information_schema, performance_schema, mysql, sys) -> multi-select checkbox list -> checkbox 'Include DROP DATABASE' (--add-drop-database, default unchecked) -> select output directory -> click Backup. Execution: sequential mariadb-dump subprocess per selected database. mariadb-dump flags: --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events (+ --add-drop-database if checked). Output filename: {dbname}_{YYYY-MM-DD_HH-mm-ss}.sql; collision: append _1, _2 etc. Progress per DB: pre-query information_schema.tables for SUM(data_length+index_length) as estimated total; ProgressReader wraps mariadb-dump stdout -> file write; emit Wails events every 250ms: {db_name, db_index, db_total, percent_estimated, mb_written, mb_per_sec, elapsed_sec}. Progress bar capped at 99% until subprocess exits 0, then jumps to 100%. Per-DB error: mark DB as failed, continue to next DB (do not stop batch). Cancel: kill current subprocess, delete partial file (auto, no prompt); if delete fails, log error + show file path. On completion: write last_op entry per DB to SQLite.
acceptance_criteria: 3 databases backed up sequentially producing 3 .sql files, progress shows ~% + MB/s + elapsed, system databases absent from list, cancel deletes partial file, failed DB marked in UI while others complete, filenames include timestamp

title: Full Restore pipeline: stream file to mariadb CLI with transformers and progress
design: UI flow: file picker -> select Server Profile -> click Restore (no Analyze step). Stream pipeline: file io.Reader -> Definer Stripper (rewrite DEFINER= to DEFINER=CURRENT_USER) -> Progress Reader (atomic byte count, emit Wails events every 100-250ms) -> mariadb CLI subprocess stdin. DROP DATABASE: pass through in Full Restore (user intent is full replacement). mariadb CLI subprocess: exec.CommandContext with cancel support; auto-discovered binary path; connection flags from selected Server Profile (-h host -P port -u user -p pass) + SSL flags if profile has SSL config. Stop-on-first-error: monitor stderr; on non-empty stderr or non-zero exit, cancel context, kill subprocess. Inline error panel: show error code + message + 'at line N' from stderr + bytes processed + Copy Error button. Cancel: context cancel -> subprocess kill -> stdin close -> file handle close. On success: write last_op entry to SQLite (operation=restore, db_name, dump_file, server_profile, timestamp, status=success). On failure: write last_op entry with status=error + error_message.
acceptance_criteria: full dump file restored to target server, Definer Stripper rewrites DEFINER clauses, progress bar shows live percentage, cancel kills subprocess with no zombie, inline error panel shows on CLI error, last_op written to SQLite

title: Byte-Offset Scanner: single-pass catalog population with Analyze UX
design: Single-slot catalog: opening a new dump file clears catalog_objects and rescans from scratch. Scanner reads with bufio.Reader, never loading full file into RAM. Multi-DB dump support: track active database via USE dbname; boundary detection. Per-table indexing: record start_byte/end_byte for DDL (CREATE TABLE) and DML (INSERT INTO) per table per database. Routines/triggers/events: record one block entry per type per database using comment markers ('-- Dumped routines for database X', '-- Dumped triggers for database X', '-- Dumped events for database X') as boundaries. catalog_objects schema: id, type (table|routines_block|triggers_block|events_block), db_name, name, start_byte, end_byte. Analyze UX: progress bar + live counter emitted via runtime.EventsEmit every 100-250ms (time.Ticker): {percent_bytes, databases_found, tables_found, routine_blocks_found}. Cancel support via context.WithCancel.
acceptance_criteria: 30GB dump scanned without OOM, multi-DB dump correctly attributes tables to databases, progress bar reaches 100%, cancel stops scan cleanly, catalog correctly populated for partial restore

title: Distribution: bundle mariadb binaries, Windows zip, Linux AppImage
design: Bundle mariadb and mariadb-dump executables with the app. Windows: include mariadb.exe, mariadb-dump.exe, libmariadb.dll in portable zip beside app binary. Linux: build AppImage using linuxdeploy + appimagetool; bundle mariadb and mariadb-dump with required shared libs. CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or equivalent): build Windows artifact (zip) and Linux artifact (AppImage). GPL compliance: About page includes MariaDB license notice with link to source. Bundled binaries placed in bin/ subdirectory beside app binary; auto-discovery checks this path first.
acceptance_criteria: Windows zip extracts and runs without any external install, Linux AppImage runs on Ubuntu 20.04+ without MariaDB pre-installed, mariadb binary found by auto-discovery in both artifacts, About page has license notice

title: Settings page: mariadb binary path config and auto-discovery
design: Settings sidebar item. On app start: auto-discover mariadb and mariadb-dump executables — Windows: Registry (HKLM SOFTWARE MariaDB*) then PATH; Linux: bundled path beside binary (AppImage), then /usr/bin/mariadb. If discovery fails, show persistent banner in Settings: 'mariadb CLI not found — configure path below'. Settings form: mariadb executable path (text field + file picker button). Path stored in SQLite app_state table. Binary path used for all Backup and Restore subprocess invocations. About page: GPL/LGPL license notice for bundled MariaDB binaries.
acceptance_criteria: auto-discovery finds bundled binary on both platforms, Settings override path is used for CLI calls, banner shown when binary not found, About page has license notice

title: Server Profile CRUD with SSL config
design: HeidiSQL-style layout: profile list (left) + form panel (right). Form fields: Display Name, Host, Port (default 3306), User, Password. SSL section: SSL Mode dropdown (Disabled | Required | Verify CA | Verify Full), CA Certificate file picker, Client Certificate file picker, Client Key file picker. Buttons: Test Connection (inline result: MariaDB version on success, error message on fail), Save (no mandatory test — untested profiles get badge). Credentials encrypted AES-GCM via app.key before writing to SQLite server_profiles table. Edit/Delete existing profiles. Selected profile persists for current session when switching to Backup or Restore panel.
acceptance_criteria: can create/edit/delete profile, Test Connection shows MariaDB version on success and error on failure, password stored encrypted in SQLite (not plaintext), untested badge visible, SSL cert paths stored

title: Partial Restore pipeline: Analyze, checklist UI, Virtual Streamer, multi-DB sequential
design: UI flow: file picker -> click Analyze -> Byte-Offset Scanner runs (progress bar + live counter) -> object checklist appears. Checklist UI: tree grouped by database; per database: individual table checkboxes + toggle 'Include routines/triggers/events for this DB'. Virtual Scroll for performance on >10,000 tables. FK warning: when user deselects a table, detect if any selected table has FK referencing it; show inline warning badge (do not block). Restore button disabled until Analyze complete and >= 1 object selected. Multi-DB selection: group selections by database. Per-database restore: synthesize header stream (SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0; SET UNIQUE_CHECKS=0; SET NAMES utf8mb4; CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS dbname; USE dbname;) + io.MultiReader of io.SectionReaders for selected byte ranges + footer stream (SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=1; COMMIT;). Stream Transformers: Definer Stripper + DROP DATABASE stripper (always strip in Partial Restore). Sequential subprocess per database: mariadb CLI with connection flags from selected Server Profile. Stop-on-first-error per subprocess: if DB N fails, do not attempt DB N+1. Progress: same inline panel as Full Restore, shows 'Restoring shop_db (1/2)'. Cancel: kill current subprocess, clean up.
acceptance_criteria: partial restore of 5 tables from 30GB dump completes without OOM, FK warning shown when referenced table deselected, multi-DB selection restores in sequence, DROP DATABASE stripped from stream, routines toggle includes/excludes routine block bytes, virtual scroll renders 10000 table list smoothly
